t: Section 375 of title 28, United States Code, is repealed.

fable.w: The section only repeals a provision of title 28 of the United States Code. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. A reference to title 28 (the judiciary title) might suggest a litigation right, but a bare repeal grants no outside party any role in a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section simply repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. Repealing a law is a legislative action that does not inherently involve participation by non-federal entities in a decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Section 375 of title 28, United States Code, is repealed.

opus.w: This section only repeals a provision of title 28. It does not require or allow the federal government to consult or coordinate with anyone outside the government before making a decision. One might guess that the repealed section involved some procedure, but its contents aren't in this text, and a bare repeal sets up no participation process.
opus.s: Section 375 of title 28, United States Code, is repealed.
opus.b:
**Step 1 – Analysis.** The section repeals a provision of title 28, the federal courts title. A reader might be tempted to guess what the repealed section did, such as setting up a commission or a procedure. But the text in front of us only deletes a provision. It does not set up consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking authority or a right to sue. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section simply repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any new requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. There is no mention of advisory boards, public hearings, comment periods, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Section 375 of title 28, United States Code, is repealed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing a statute could implicitly remove a participation requirement, or that the repeal itself is a decision involving outside parties. However, the text provided is merely a statement of repeal. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or coordination with non-federal entities. It is a legislative action affecting the code, not a procedural requirement for participation in a federal decision-making process involving outsiders.
